title: Solid product, just not for our cars...
text:
The WizGear Magnetic Mount comes with 2 rectangular (2 5/8" x 2 3/4") and 2 round (1 1/2") metal disks with adhesive backing for mounting on your dashboard or other flat surface, as well as additional rectangular and circular stickers, and 2 super strong magnets with rubber prongs to attach to your car vent blades. The product is solidly made and very strong, however, it did not work for our car configurations. Things to consider when purchasing these are the orientation of your fan blades (horizontal vs. vertical), whether the vents lean forward or backward (which makes a huge difference when the sun is out), range of motion of the vents so you can move your phone/gps to the left or right, size of phone, etc.

In my video, I show the challenges we had using these in both of our cars - a Hyundai Santa Fe and a Hyundai Tuscon. The Tuscon has smaller vents with vertical blades. The Santa Fe has slightly larger vents with horizontal blades. I took the video in the early evening. It was still sunny out but the cars where in the shade. The glare doesn't appear to be a huge issue in the video but it is killer when the sun is beating on your dashboard. When we originally tried these, it was sunny out and you couldn't see anything on the screen due to the angle of the vent and the glare of the sunlight. As I note in the video, if your vents are further to the right of the steering wheel and not angle too far forward, these may work for you. These did not work for us and we will be going with the kind that has the gel bottom that clings to the dashboard or window without adhesives.

text:
Update (2/15/2019):
18 months in service and the rubber grip on one of them has ripped and the metal prongs are poking through where it touches the vent. See photos. Dropping 2 stars.

My first time using one of these magnetic mounts. Love that it comes in a 2-pack: one for each of our cars. I primarily got it so I had somewhere to stash my phone while driving instead of in the cup holder. Works great when using phone as GPS device. In our SUV, the angle is perfect. I can see the screen clearly with no glare from the sun. In the sedan, it's angled upwards just enough that the screen is slightly washed out by the sun. Not terrible enough to return this but annoying.

The back of the magnet mounts have a thin slit and a thick slit to accomodate different size vents. Pkg comes with 4 metal plates (2 small circles and 2 big rectangles). The rectangles are great for flatback phones such as the iPhone. My LG G4 has a curved back so I use the small circle. The rectangle is just big enough that it causes my phone case to not fit snugly. The metal plates have adhesive on the back but I don't use it. The plates stay put between the case and phone. This way I can swap it out when I get a new phone. To fix the angled issue mentioned above, I eventually moved the metal plate down and to the side (instead of centered on the phone's back) and this changed the angle enough to work for me. Good thing I didn't use the adhesive, right?

title: Overall a good product, a couple of cons
text: I ordered this product for my iPhone 6 Plus. The product came with 2 round receiver magnets to attach to car heating/air vents, 2 magnetic rectangle plates and 2 magnetic circle plates to stick on your phone or in your phone case, and 2 rectangle and 2 circle sticker films (I can't figure out what these are for- maybe to keep the magnets from rubbing on your phone case?). The plates have a paper, like the back of a sticker, which if pulled off would expose a sticky side of the magnet which you could use to attach the plates to your phone or your case. I did not peel them off because the plates stay in my phone case just fine once the case is on with no need to stick them. This way, I can move them from case to case when I switch. I use a thin cosmetic case on my phone, and since my phone is so large I placed 2 of the 4 thin magnetic plates in my phone case and then put the case back on. Even though my case is thin, I cannot feel or see the magnets. I drive a Toyota Prius, and I placed one receiver magnet on the vent on the driver's side, and the other on the passenger side (for me to use while my husband is driving).  I am impressed with the strongness of the magnets and how well they snap together considering how paper thin the plates are. They aren't easy to pull apart from the receiver bases. My phone stays stuck while driving, even on bumpy roads. You could use this one kit for two phones in two separate cars if you wanted to. The only con, for me, is that the receiver magnets don't hold on to my vents as securely as I wish they did. Sometimes when I grab my phone off quickly, the receiver magnet comes off the vent and comes with my phone. I wish there was some way to make them stay on the vents a little better. Even so, overall I am very happy with this product, especially for less than $10! It makes it so easy to keep your phone within reach and view while driving when using it for navigation. It sure beats throwing the phone on the passenger seat or in the cup holders.  EDIT: After using these for about a week in the 100 degree summer weather, I've noticed another con.The magnetic base itself blocks about half of my cool air vent, which prevents half of my cool air from blowing on me in the 100 degree car. Worse, when my phone is on the base, my large phone blocks the entire air vent! This may not bother some people, especially those who typically direct the air flow away from themselves when driving, but I use the cool air from the vent as a fan pointed directly on me in the summer. EDIT #2: I recently switched to a phone case that has a clear back, and can't use the magnets with it because they show and look dumb. I am now searching for a non-magnetic car phone holder until I switch to another (not clear) case.

title: Magnet Too Strong For My GPS
text:
I bought this mount for my Garmin Nuvi 275. I was a little reluctant to buy it at first because I feared the magnet would affect the operation of my GPS. But after reading some of the positive reviews, I decided to order a set. The first problem I faced was the limited space between the back of the mount and my car vent. With no power cable, it was fine. But if I plugged the power cable in (which I have to do in order to get traffic updates), I had to retract the mount from the vent to the point where it was barely grasping.

The second (and most disappointing) problem I faced was that the magnet caused the GPS to continue to lose satellite reception. Basically, my GPS becomes useless when the magnet is attached to the back. So, in my case, the mount was a waste of money. Perhaps it works better with cell phones but I'm not even going to try.

title: Great for the price
text:
I gave this 5 stars not because it's perfect, because it isn't, but because it's just so easy to use, so versatile (it comes with sticky tape, but I don't want it to be a "permanent" installation), and so cheap. I wanted it for GPS driving directions, and with this little gadget I can use it for navigating as either the driver or the passenger. I'm currently using one of these as a driver in a Ford F-150 truck. The choices for air vents are not optimal. If I put it on the one to the right of the driver, I knock the phone off when I shift gears. If I put it farther to the right, to the left of the passenger, then it swivels around every time I go around a curve and I have to bring it back to face me. Also, it's really too far to tell what's going on with the phone.

So I ended up putting it to the left of the driver near the window. That cuts off cool air on hot days when the sun comes in that window, but everything else is good. I managed to install it in such a way that it doesn't swivel, and the phone gets braced against a knob underneath (lights, I think - which don't come into play as often as shifting) so I can easily touch the screen if I need to. I can see directions if using Google Maps, and I can also easily see who's calling or texting.

We also have a Prius, and I'll come back later to update this after I have used the gadget in that car.

They do hold, but, when using the GPS function in the landscape position in the car, the phone will NOT hold on the mount due to the imbalance caused by the low installed plate, nor is it very stable.
I really like the mounts but this is a hassle and I do not have a further solution.

title: Road bumps and vibration will cause this vent clip to fail and your phone to fall
text:
The vent clips are just about useless. They do not grip tight enough to secure itself to the vent blades, causing the phone to at first drop its angle from mere road vibration and then the clip completely detaches from the vent if you hit even the slightest bump. I have another vent mount that grips the phone case with a spring-clamp and it connects securely to the vent blades, but really wanted a magnet version for easier mounting of the phone so I tried this product. The magnet is great. I actually own a visor clip WizGear with the same magnet and don't have any complaint about the magnet strength at all (and I keep the metal plate between the phone and the outer case). Its definitely the fault of the vent clip that makes this product unusable. I have a vent with single rows of vent blades. Someone who has a vent with a grid design may have better luck with this product since it can connect on the horizontal and vertical axis.

I ended up going with a magnet mount that connects with an adhesive pad directly to the dash. [[ASIN:B0721D4NPP Maxboost Magnetic Car Mount, (3-Pack) Universal Flat Stick-on Dashboard Holder +Metal Plate/ADH-Tape for Phone iPhone X, iPhone 8 7 PLUS,Galaxy s8 Note,HTC,Pixel,LG G6,GPS,Phablet (Work w/ most Case)]]. I actually still use it on the vent. I closed the vent and attached the adhesive pad to the closed vent. When I rotate the vent I still have enough clearance to rotate it completely without the magnetic mount blocking its movement.

title: Cheap and strong magnet.
text:
Been wanting to buy one of these for years. I'm not into the whole pop-sockets and things that you glue to stick to your phone cover to even on the outside of your case. I like a clean look and I like my phone in my pocket. So getting something that wouldn't protrude from the phone was a must. I was skeptical of the magnet strength but when I got it installed was very pleased. I also didn't want to stick or glue anything to my car so something that hooked to the air vents was a must.

I read the reviews and one said to take the piece that sticks to your phone and just place it between your phone cover and the phone itself. You can peal and stick it to the back of you phone but if you ever change phones you'll need to use another sticky pad. It might slide around a little but I used the larger pad and don't have issues with where to put on the car mount. The installation of the car mount it pretty easy. Depending on your air vents it may work out to be in the perfect spot or not. For my car it's in a great spot. The car mount also seems solid and in place.

Overall it's a great way to get your phone up and in better sight if you need GPS or any music controls. That's pretty much what I use it for. For the money this also seemed to be the cheapest option. In all pretty happy with this purchase and would highly recommend.

Update 5-13-19:
So over a year later and this is still a great product. I even put one of the mounts in my wife's car. It's quite different that my car and the vent is at sharper angle but nonetheless still works good. I bought a new car this year and it still fits well on the vent. I use it just about ever time I get into the car. It's very handy to use and much safer if you need to use your phone. I even switched phones. I did stick the magnet that goes on the phone onto the inside of the phone case. If you change cases you'll have to remember to take it out. But you could, just as I did before, put the magnet between the case and the phone. I stuck it to the case because the magnet does move and I feel like I could easily remove (if I remember) it when or if I change cases. I still love that there is nothing sticking out from the phone the magnet is really strong. Highly recommend this as a cheap and easy way to mount your phone in your car.

title: Awesome phone mount, easy installation, great price
text:
Very cool product and good price. The circular magnet fits fine between my iPhone SE and a Speck brand case. There are little plastic covers (like packing tape) included in the kit and I put one over the magnet in my phone case to avoid scratching the back of the phone.

Installed in one of the center vents in my car below the radio, never falls off during driving. Very easy to remove the phone from the magnet when needed. If you're blasting the heat through these vents it can make the phone a little hot - I just shut off the air flow to that specific vent when the phone is installed.

The clips on the back of the magnet have two different widths depending on how wide the vent is that you're installing it on. Take note of this and be careful not to press it on too hard when installing - if the width of the clip is not a good fit for the vent you might damage the vent. As noted, look at the size of the clip width compared to where you're installing it before trying to force it on.

title: Lasts a year
text: It worked very well for more than 6 months. As the weight of the phone starts bearing on the grip behind, they start to grow apart slowly. I rotated the grip so that the AC vent is in between different two grips and it worked for some time until they started to grow apart. Within a year, the four grips are now so far apart, that it falls off the AC vent if I put my phone on it and go over a speed breaker or uneven road. By the way, important thing to note is that it took 1 year for it to get to this stage with using an iPhone 6s. If your phone is heavy or light, I guess there would be appropriate time difference. title: I'm stuck on this product.
text:
Okay, I admit I was a little leery of using something with magnets that attached to a smart phone. Something about magnets and electronics and data didn't sit too well with me. So I put off buying one of these. I had been using a suction-cup cell phone holder in my car. The suction cup wouldn't work on the dash, only on the windshield. But I didn't like having the phone stuck to the windshield and partially obscuring my field of view.

After reading many reviews from others about how easy to use this product was (and noticing that no one was writing about the magnet erasing critical data from their smartphones, I decided to give this a shot. I am glad I did. This comes with two magnetic mounts so I plan on giving one to my son for use in his car. Attaching the phone to the magnet couldn't be simpler and the phone does NOT move or slide once attached. I have had no issues driving down the road worrying about the phone coming off and falling to the floor of the car.

I purposely did not use the adhesive to attach the magnetic plate to the back of my phone. I didn't want any sticky residue left behind if I decided I didn't want to use the product after a while. So, I simply slid the magnetic plate inside my phone's protective after-market cover and it works like a champ. My phone cover fits my phone well and the magnetic plated does not slide around inside. I couldn't be happier. The added plus is that, on really hot days, the magnetic mount is attached to the AC vent on my dashboard - the phone is readily visible without being in the way of any of the car controls and has the added bonus of being cooled by the AC as I toodle down the road. Great little product!

title: Does it's job / Can't position air flow
text: These definitely work and work well but they're kinda a pain in the butt. Let me explain... The magnet mounts fit well and stay sturdy in the air vents of our 2016 Honda Odyssey and 2018 VW Jetta. The magnet "sticker" that goes on the phone keeps a strong hold onto the mount. We didn't use the actual sticker, we just placed the magnet in between our cell phone and the case (in other words, it's being held in place "on" the phone because it's sitting inside the case). This has worked well with both our iPhone 6s and iPhone 8 Plus. So these get the job done. However, the pain in the butt part... the way they fit onto the vent makes it difficult to adjust the vent position. It's basically impossible for me to get these onto the vent in a way that holds my phone so that I can see it AND allows the vent to blow air in my direction. If you don't care about the air flow, then these are great! But if you live in Florida, like me, you may want to make sure your a/c is able to blow in your direction and, in that case, you may find these to be a little inconvenient, as I did.

title: Sometimes the simplest solution is often the best solution. That is certainly the case with the ...
text:
Sometimes the simplest solution is often the best solution. That is certainly the case with the WizGear Magnetic Car Mounts. I had a couple of phone mounts for my car in recent years, and they all suffered from the same basic design flaw: springs will inevitably become loose, plastic teeth will slowly wear down , and after a while a plastic contraption that—when you first bought it—held your phone sturdily in place ,won’t even be able to secure it if you go over a small speed bump.
Using a magnetic mount is so much simpler and intuitive. Instead of getting in your car and trying to secure your phone with some type of over complicated clasp, just put it near the magnet and you’re good to go. Really, it’s that simple: attach the magnetic strip to your phone, attach the mount to your car’s air vent, and you're set. While other mounts I used ceased to function after only a couple of months (or even weeks), the WizGear is still going strong.
There’s really not much else to say about this thing. If you want a no hassle solution to mounting your phone in your vehicle, just pick these things up. And in case you were wondering, I have an IPhone 8 Plus, which is definitely one of the larger and heavier phones out there, and the WizGear holds in place just fine. It comes with two mounts and two magnetic strips, so should you lose one or want to share it with a spouse, family member, or friend, you’re covered. For the selling price, you really can’t go wrong.

title: My favorite mount type - just forget about wireless charging
text:
I've bought several of these packs now and I am fairly confident they are one of the best options for nonobstrusive car mounting. You place one of 2 sizes of magnets either directly adhered to your phone back or in the space between your case and your phone, squeeze the receiving end onto your car vent, then just through the phone up and you're good to go! I find it much more convenient that the hinge-style mounts (bulkier), and I wouldn't even consider the mounts with the long arms (way too obtrusive).
The key to these products, though, is their ability to successfully hold up your phone. As phones get heavier, the challenge is greater. I had a set from a year ago that didn't seem to hold my new iPhone X well at all. I lost it in a rental car and had to buy a new replacement, which works much better! They must have increased the magnet strength. Now it easily holds up my phone+apple leather case without a problem. When it's plugged it, I do find that it can't quiet withstand the slightly downward torque from the cable, so I find ways to make the cable extend perpendicularly from the vent and it works fine. My second criticism is purely due to the design of this type of mount-- the magnet will block your Qi wireless capability. I managed for a while to place the magnet in such a way that I could still get charging, but the error rate was too high so I opted to keep the mount and forgo the wireless charging.

title: Opioid Crisis strikes Amazon
text:
I was really interested in purchasing these magnets after seeing over 9,000 reviews and 4.5 star rating. However, I saw a video showing that a knockoff was delivered instead of an original. That led me to read the reviews and they all seemed great, until I sorted by most recent reviews. Wow! What a difference. I'm so disappointed in what I read.

One can only speculate as to the rise and fall of the makers of this product. They more than likely sold thousands of these and only paid cents to make them. Life was great! Limo rides to "Da Club" and "Poppin bottles in da ice". Then a shadowy figure comes along and offers a "really good time". Who can say no when you're on top of the world. "Cocaine is one hell of a drug" as Rick James would say. Sure, it's all fun and games living the high Life. But your product was so good, that eventually you have no more new customers. You begin to run out of the once steady income. You go to a cheaper supplier so that you can support your luxurious life style. You save a few more cents off the dollar, but that's not enough to keep the party going. You start craving the high Life with no satisfaction.

The shadowy figure returns. You can't afford the powder anymore. "Hey, I got a cheaper option for you" he says. The H works for the first few times but then everything starts spiraling down hill. Before you know it, there are no more responses to customer concern or complaints. You just throw pieces that you have lying around and ship it to anyone for a quick score. It's truly an epidemic. I hope there is recovery in the near future. Again, this is only a speculation. I hope to see some recent positive reviews so that I can make a confident purchase. I don't like having to call, complain or return items.

Amazon, if there is no recovery, please remove the seller. No one wants a bad seller affecting your awesome site!

title: Strong grip! My phone hasn’t fallen off once!
text:
I absolutely love this product. I’ve tried suction cups, I’ve tried the ones you stick in the air vent and it holds the phone in like, those bracket things. But nothing has ever worked until this magnet!
It comes with four magnet strips to attached to your phone. I actually put the strips between my phone and phone case, rather than on the outside of my phone case. I didnt want to lose it and it also wouldn’t have looked good.
With my older iPhone 5S I only put one of the magnetic strips between my case and phone and the slip would slide around gradually and eventually sink to the bottom half of my phone. This wasn’t a huge issue.

When I updgraded to the iPhone 8 I decided to put two of the magnetic strips between my phone and phone case because this phone is bigger and if the magnet shifted it would be a problem. I took the magnetic strip that was sticky and stuck it on the upper half of the inside of my phone case, and put the non sticky magnetic strip on the bottom half. Now the entire back of my phone is covered and it is way more secure on the holder (not that this was an issue).

The magnet held my iPhone 5S with no problems and it continues to hold my iPhone 8 with no problems. I did notice that the magnet’s grips that hold it in the air vent seems to get loose? But that’s easily resolved by taking out the magnet and rotating it.

I have a VW CC and the vents are just fine with it. I also bought one for my agency vehicle because I couldn’t live with out it. I’ve used it in a Kia van, Honda vans, Honda CRV/HRV and one of the little Honda cars, Dodge vans, and a Nissan Maxima with no problems.

I also have no issues with charging my phone. I saw that some people have? I’m not sure how the magnetic strips would cause an issue when you’re charging your phone. The strips themselves are not magnets; they can’t stick to the fridge. So I’m not sure there’s any need for worry. I haven’t had any issues!

I’ve bought these for so many people now that I’ve lost track. It’s such a great little tool! Definitely get it!

While neither device stays in place on a single mount in a moving car, I was able to get a stable experience using both of the mounts to hold my iPhone in place.
On the other hand, I couldn’t get my MotoG5 S Plus to stay secured even when I used both mounts and it kept slipping off with the vibrations from the road as the car was driving, almost damaging my phone.
Not very powerful I would say and definitely not worth the money.

Update:
I received follow up emails form the ‘wizgear’ and I reached out to them to which I received a prompt response; adding a star for courteous customer service. The service representative advised me about stronger magnetic mounts (with a bigger profile, more magnets and larger metal plates) they sell on Amazon. From what I see those should serve people with bigger and heavier phones better but run about the same cost for one as you would spend on two of these smaller round mounts, worthwhile options for someone with a bigger phone.

text:
Overall this is a good quality product with just a few problems.

I bought this magnetic mount because in my job I rarely get the same vehicle twice and I needed a way to mount my phone temporary no matter what car I was in. For this issue, the magnetic vent mount solves my problem. As I switch cars a lot another nice feature is having the second mount in case I lose one or forget to grab it when turning in the car. The price is also attractive as I am not too worried if I lose one. But now to the flaws, The first flaw is obvious as it is a vent mount it does cover the vent, so It along with your phone do block a lot of the heat or cooling coming from that vent. I knew this when making the purchase so it's not a huge deal but it is an issue. My second complaint is that there really is no retaining mechanism so when I go to remove my phone many times the mount comes off the vent along with the phone.While it is not difficult to reinstall it does become a pain at times. Overall this is a good quality product with a few inherent design flaws.

Pro
Good quality product with a fairly strong magnet.
Comes with 2 magnetic mounts good for 2 cars.
A simple design that will work in most vehicles.
Easily transferable to another vehicle.

Con
Blocks heat or cooling from the vent.
The magnet is stronger than prongs that attach to vent and the mount is removed many times when you go to retrieve your phone.

title: Longevity might be an issue...
text:
I've had this product for more than a year and use it during my daily commute along with anytime I'm driving. Installation is about as easy as it comes and the adhesive used for the metal plate (phone side) is very durable. In fact, you can likely pull it off of your phone and reapply it with little degradation to how securely it attaches. The magnets in the mount side are also very strong.
Here's the only issue I've run into: the mounts lose their ability to hold onto the AC vent over time. The rubber will eventually develop memory of the AC vent width and then it becomes useless. Having included two in the set does mean that once the first goes, you do have a backup (if you haven't been using both) but do expect this to happen. Simply put, this is a consumable item and will not be a one time purchase. At $12 (what I paid), that isn't much to complain about.
However, purchasing a more conventional holder does afford you benefits that can't be found here:
-The mount is probably going to last longer
-You don't lose wireless charging due to the metal plate

High marks for simplicity, low marks for longevity. If you buy this, you will need to buy again at some point in time.

title: Hands down, this is the best cell phone car mount!
text:
UPDATE #2: Came to Amazon to buy new magnetic plates for a new phone and figured I’d update my review to mention that it’s now been almost 4 years since my purchase and I still love the simplicity of this car mount. I especially love how it still works with a a Love Handle strap attached to the case (read review for details). I originally used it with an iPhone 7 Plus and now use it with an iPhone 13.

UPDATE #1: 2 years later and still love this car mount.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I’ve used a few different car mounts, including magnetic types and none of them even come close to how simple and easy this one is to use.

A prior magnetic car mount I used came with a bulky magnet that went on my phone and a similar magnet that clipped onto to the vent. However, the magnet that was attached to my phone damaged every credit/debit card I owned as I often carry my wallet against my phone in one hand. The magnet on my phone apparently interfered with the magnetic strips.

The other mount I used is the type that has tension arms that hugs your phone, which then attaches via a vent clip. Having an iPhone 6 Plus and now a 7 Plus, it really pushed the arm tension to the max. I would have to remove the mount from the vent to squeeze my phone into the arms each time I used it and often, the mount would come off the vent when trying to release my phone. As a result, the rubber on the prongs began to stretch, tear and bunch up into the gaps meant for the vent. I tried to cut it back but then it wouldn’t fit snuggly and the revealed metal scratched the plastic vent.

When that mount broke, I ordered this one, making sure that the magnetic plates did not affect the magnetic strips of debit/credit cards. I’ve had this mount for over a year now and it hasn’t damaged a single one.

Since my phone is large and heavy, I positioned both magnetic plates horizontally within the inside of my phone’s case, which is a decently thick hard shell case. This ensures that almost the entire back side of my phone can be attached to the car mount so I can plop it on without having to readjust it.

One vent clip magnet did the trick and steadily held my iPhone 7 Plus. But then without thinking, I purchased and installed a “Love Handle”. It’s basically an eslastic loop used to hold my phone for one hand typing, and is attached via a 2.5”x1” inch plastic adhesive piece. I installed it in the center, vertically just over an inch down from the Apple logo so it comes down to about half an inch from the bottom. Needless to say, the added a 2.5” long and 1” wide uneven surface disrupted the force between the magnetic plates in my case and the vent clip magnet.

BUT! I remembered this came with two vent magnets so I attached one on the far left of my vent and the other on the far right which created a gap of just over 1 inch. Now, my Love Handle fits comfortably in this gap and the magnets hold onto my phone perfectly. My phone has NEVER fallen off the mount, which is impressive consindering how large and heavy my phone is, especially with the case. I’ve included pictures of my setup in the event you can’t picture it (my car is due for a cleaning). The magnets are so strong that I still can position my phone horizontally without issues, even with the uneven surface created by the Love Handle.

The best part? There is no wear and tear since I’ve NEVER had to reinstall these vent magnets so the rubber hasn’t worn or stretched at all.

As you can tell, I love this car mount and highly recommend it to anyone looking to buy one!

title: My current favorite in the search for a usable phone-holding solution!
text:
I've purchased several types of holders for my digital devices, and this one seems to be the most versatile and easy-to-use. I primarily use this for my Nexus 6, which is one of the larger Android phones, one which I've had difficulty fitting into spring-loaded holders which barely accommodate it.

These holders get around that problem by using a strong magnetic attraction to a plate that's slipped between my phone's case and the body, making it very easy to both mount and dismount the device in a blink of an eye!

They're designed with closely-spaced, split tapered rubber prongs with are inserted into the vanes of air conditioning vents on your car's dash. I was a little skeptical about their ability to remain in place, but haven't had any incidents where it's come loose and appeared in danger of falling out. The strength of the magnet is sufficient that I'm confident that it won't accidentally separate from the holder from vibration.

They should work in most vent-mounting scenarios, but there may be exceptions, especially on smaller vents. You have to make sure that the round magnet mounting surface will clear the directional vane 'switch' to insert the holder into the vent, and also that the face of the magnet sticks out more than the switch so that the phone can fit to the magnet properly. It wasn't a problem in my application, and I tried it in two different locations in my vehicle.

With the vent mount, you'll lose a bit of cool air in the summer, with it partially obstructed by the phone, but the flip side is that your phone doesn't run quite as warm as it can get in a car when it's in use.

One thing that may -- or may not be -- obvious, is that you should avoid pulling your device straight away from the magnet, as this would be more likely to partially remove the holder at the same time. I simply slide my phone up, down, or to the side until the magnet and base plate are no longer aligned, and it comes off very easily without dislodging the rubber prongs.

About the only negative I've observed at this point is that, in a rough-riding vehicle, like a pickup truck, vibrations can cause the phone to rotate out of position slightly, as it's only being held in place by magnetic forces applied between two smooth surfaces. This isn't a huge deal, and it's easily corrected. It can also be mitigated somewhat by attaching the base plate to the phone in a location where the weight and geometry of the phone would discourage this movement. For example, putting the base plate towards the top of the device would result in the more of the phone's mass being below the center of the magnet, and it would tend to hang straighter, with less rotation.

Bottom-line: These work for my situation, and I'm very please to finally find an acceptable solution.

title: Sturdy one-piece clip, extremely low profile can make placement a challenge.
text:
I received exactly what I was looking for with this magnetic phone holder: a one-piece, low profile design with magnetic inserts.

The package comes with two identical and complete setups: two round metal adhesive plates (with backings), two rectangular metal adhesive plates (with backings), and two magnetic (rubberized plastic) one-piece phone holders to stick in your car vents.

The phone holders are actually two pieces, but are constructed in a way that they will not come apart unless you are purposely trying to break them, so there is no worry of a clip or part slipping off and getting lost in your vehicle. This was a must for me, and something I was unable to find in any store for similarly designed products. Additionally, this product was cheaper, more sturdily constructed, and came as a double-set.

I wouldn't expect this to hold my phone as I'm jumping over railroad tracks, but as long as my phone doesn't end up under the gas pedal while I'm driving, I'm pretty happy.

The magnets are strong enough when used appropriately with the metal plates, with any distance between the two causing a decrease in ability to hold the phone (case). I attached two rectangular metal plates to the inside back of my armored phone case, not the phone. It provided the greatest versatility in mounting with all vent locations in my vehicle.

If you have recessed vents in your car, beveled vent edges, very short vent blades, or a small vent area and a protruding vent damper, then this phone holder will likely not work for your setup. It is very low profile, about 0.75 cm or 0.5 inch. If the phone rests against the bevels surrounding your vents or the vent damper, it will not rest against the magnet, and the magnet will not make a good connection with the metal plates. The setup will never hold.

I would not recommend this magnetic phone holder, or any similar phone holder to a person with a magnetic phone charger unless you are certain you can place the metal plates in an area that will not interfere with the area designated for wireless magnetic charging. Likely, you will not be able to magnetically charge with the phone holder in place, even if clearance allows...and it probably won't.

The two sizes of vent slots on each of the magnetic phone holders should fit most vehicles. They are rubberized, fairly long, and they slowly taper to a thick pyramid-type shape. They won't easily break, unless you're a monster. I could imagine the wide slot sliding on vertical vents, but not if you jammed the narrow slot onto the vent louvers.

title: Worked perfectly!
text: These devices worked perfectly on our iPhone 8 work phones.  Despite our phones being in Ghostek waterproof cases and some rough jostles over potholes and such, they never once separated from the magnetic mounts, nor did the mount itself dislodge from the air vent.  The metal plates, even the small ones, did interfere with and prevent the wireless charging feature of our phones if the plate was located in the middle of the phone where the wireless charging coil is located.  Moving the metal plate to the top, or bottom, end of the phone solved that issue.  We did notice that if the metal plate was located at the bottom of the phone, the phone would tend to drift/twist when jostled due to it being a bit top heavy...but simply placing the phone upside down on the mount, so most of the weight was below the mount, solved that little problem.  All in all...an excellent, low profile, solution for mounting phones to air vents where you can actually see them when using GPS/maps.

text: The instructions leave a bit to be desired, delving into the techno-babble somewhat with regards to where to attach the magnet on the phone side. I opted to put it on the outside of my case, where it attached well and has stayed well while extruding a minimal amount. On the car side, this is a large magnet that blocks much of your vent. A helpful design addition would be a couple of flaps, like wings, that deflects the air that hits the back of the product to redirect the air into the vehicle better. There are two different widths to clip onto your vent. It stays on virtually all of the time. Be sure to check it once in awhile to make sure it's still in. Mine has never popped out while in motion. My luck with other types of "solutions" to this, which have included a vent clip that had a clip that "grasps" your phone (it was built cheaply, though a freebie that a friend got at a conference seems to work well for them), the stick-on attachment to a dashboard, and a weighted base that rests on - but can still slide around on - a dashboard have failed. As for "Security features," I don't know what this refers to, for as far as I can tell, there aren't any! In summary, this is a movable solution (from vent to vent or car to car) that works!

title: Keeps my phone close by for nav assistance while remaining hands-free.
text:
I live in a state where it’s against the law to be using a cellphone while driving, but I also rely heavily on my GPS app to help me navigate the roads. I heard about this magnetic phone mount from a relative, and their overall satisfaction with this product was all the encouragement I needed to try it for myself. The mount holds onto your phone by connecting to a second magnetic piece (which is included) that you stick onto the back of the phone case, and you can apply that magnetic piece at the top, bottom, or middle, wherever it’s most convenient. The magnetic piece has an adhesive backing, so it’ll stay on your phone until you decide to pry it off. Next, you take the mounted piece and shove it in-between your air vent panel’s little slats (either on the driver’s side or passenger’s side) and basically ‘snap’ the phone onto the mount by connecting the magnets!

To remove the phone from the mount, just grab the phone and slide it one way or another to pull the magnets apart - once the panel on the back of your phone has completely cleared the magnet on the mount, you can then just lift your phone away and go about using it normally. The magnetic connection is pretty dang strong, which is good when you need your phone to be secured while driving, but it was surprising to realize how much effort I had to put it to pull the magnets apart, too. When the company tells you that their mount maintains a strong connection to your phone while in use, they’re definitely not kidding.

This product has made it super easy for me to keep my phone nearby whenever I’m driving, even if I don’t need navigation to find where I’m going. It also keeps my screen just off in my periphery so I can quickly see any incoming calls or notifications, so I can continue paying full attention to what’s really important - driving. 10/10 - I would definitely recommend this product to anyone who still needs an effective and SAFE hands-free method for their vehicle. I say ‘still’ because honestly, it’s 2021, road safety should already be our number-one priority. We should ALL be keeping 100% of our attention on the road whenever operating a vehicle. The phone calls and texts can wait; this magnetic car mount keeps your phone nearby without being a distraction.

title: Easy, simple, works! Safe driving
text:
What’s not to love? I’ve purchased these several times now, for myself and loved ones. I’ve tried other mounts or holders, and this is by far the best. It’s small, there’s zero “installation”; you just pop it into your vent, and stick one of the magnets to the back of your phone case. It’s so easy to pop your phone right onto it as soon as you get in the car, so there’s no worry about rooting around for your phone while driving, and most importantly not taking your eyes off the road while still being able to see your Maps app.

Now, I am horrified if I see a friend or family member looking at their phone while driving with it in there hand. The difference between glancing down at your hand, and it being already in your line of vision is HUGE. Also, it’s easy to bring the mount with you if you’ll be using someone else’s car or a rental for travel. The only downside is that because it fixes into your vent, if it is super hot out, sometimes I take my phone off it so the air can blow directly on me from that vent and not be partially blocked by my phone; as well as in the winter, if I have to blast the heat I am definitely going to take my phone off it temporarily til the car heats up enough that I can switch the vent to mostly floor vents, so that it won’t heat up my phone. But those occasions are few enough that it isn’t a big deal to me overall. And you get TWO, for an amazing price. They last years, I can’t see what could go wrong, they’re magnets so there’s nothing that could break or die. So go ahead and buy these!! :):):)

text:
I’ve had this mount for about a year and a half now, so I figured I’m overdue for a review.

I actually really love this mount. I’ve had the same mount with the same original magnets that it came out with and they haven’t let me down yet. The magnets that come with the product, I put inside my case, so a silicone and plastic case in between the magnet and the mount hasn’t stopped it from keeping my phone mounted with no issues.

I’ve noticed here recently the magnets power has started to dye down. I dont know if it’s the mount magnet, or the phone magnet…. but for the price of these, o don’t mind just put hazing a new one. I didn’t expect it to last this long anyways, and for something that isn’t “top dollar” buying a new one after a year and a half isn’t a big deal at all. Also, by now they have newer model products and have probably made stronger products….. so I’d be happy to stay loyal to their brand and see if they have something I might enjoy using better till it starts to die on me over time and do it all over again.

I bought some for my mom and gave my second set (which I haven’t used, and could have used to last another year and a half), to my husband and they also really like them. So I’d recommend this product to anyone.

I’d say the only downside is because I took it off and put it on and changed locations of the mount many times to accommodate watching movies with someone while eating in the parking lot after using drive thru, or letting someone use it in the car to watch something on my phone since I have CarPlay and don’t need to use my actual phone for GPS, it’s scratched the vent up some. Although, if you put it in and dont feel you ever need to move it, that won’t happen. AND as I said, they could have made improvements since my original purchase in October 2020.

So, if we need to use one at any point we will have to remove our phone cases before charging. Maybe I did something wrong, but that was our experience with both of our phones.
